predecessors.name: Khmer Empire
predecessors.text: the Khmer realm of 1431 as Cliopatria draws it, with the court moving from Angkor to the Phnom Penh area

successors.name: French Indochina
successors.text: Cambodia under King Norodom, a French protectorate from 11 August 1863; the monarchy stays in place

ledger.x: 1432: after the Siamese intervention at Angkor, King Ponhea Yat holds the Khmer lands from the Phnom Penh area.
1525: Ang Chan I moves the capital from Phnom Penh to Longvek (infobox 'Longvek (1525-1594)'; the text gives no year).

1594: the Siamese capture and sack Longvek ('In 1594, Longvek was successfully captured and sacked by Siamese forces') and the court moves to Srey Sarchor (Srei Santhor), infobox 'Srey Sarchor (1594-1620)'.
1658: the Vietnamese intervene in Cambodia for the first time.
1699: the delta passes under Vietnamese administration.
1700: the Mekong delta is lost to the Nguyễn lords.
1795: Siam annexes Battambang and Siem Reap.
1847: Nguyen rule ends (infobox 'Nguyen rule: 1834-1847'); the page then has Cambodia 'placed under joint suzerainty between the two regional empires' (Siam and Vietnam), undated.

wars.name: Siamese capture of Longvek
wars.outcome: Longvek was captured and sacked by Siamese forces in 1594 and the court moved to Srey Sarchor; no border change is recorded on the page.

wars.name: Vietnamese settlement and intervention in the Mekong delta
wars.outcome: Vietnamese settlers reached the delta by 1620, a custom-post followed at Prey Nokor (Saigon) about 1623, the first military intervention came in 1658-59, and by the end of the 17th century the delta was under full Vietnamese administrative control.

wars.name: Siamese annexation of Battambang and Siem Reap
wars.outcome: Siam annexed Battambang and Siem Reap in 1795.

wars.name: Vietnamese occupation of Cambodia (Tây Thành)
wars.outcome: Nguyen rule from 1834 to 1847 with a rebellion in 1840-1841; Cambodia then stood under joint Siamese-Vietnamese suzerainty.

certainty.note: No treaty or survey fixes any frontier on the pages opened; the Mekong delta, the north-west and the Cham/highland edge are approximate.
